findings.title: AuthzClient.create() can install a stub CryptoProvider process-wide
findings.body: CryptoIntegration is a process-wide singleton, initialized once on the first call to init(). AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). If the authz-client jar is on the classpath, the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) is only chosen when no higher-order provider is present. Any application that creates an AuthzClient before keycloak-crypto-default or keycloak-crypto-fips is initialized will have CryptoIntegration.getProvider() return AuthzClientCryptoProvider for the rest of the JVM. Most of its methods (getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getSignature, getAesGcmCipher, etc.) throw UnsupportedOperationException, so unrelated Keycloak crypto code later in the same JVM fails at runtime. The ordering-based selection only protects the case where the other providers are already on the classpath.

findings.title: New abstract method order() breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation
findings.body: order() is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Every third-party or in-tree implementation of CryptoProvider that does not implement it will fail to compile and, if it was compiled earlier, fail with AbstractMethodError at runtime. A default implementation (for example returning a neutral value) would keep the existing contract working. The PR does not show that all implementations in the repository (including test code) were updated.

findings.title: Providers with equal order are chosen nondeterministically and silently
findings.body: detectProvider sorts providers by order() descending and takes the first. DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200. If two of them are on the classpath, the winner depends on ServiceLoader iteration order, which is not defined. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException for multiple providers, which made this misconfiguration visible. Now it is silently accepted, and the choice of crypto backend (FIPS vs non-FIPS) can change between runs or deployments. Ties should be rejected or resolved explicitly.

findings.title: Ignored provider list is logged as a format string
findings.body: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) passes a computed string as the format pattern. If any provider class name contains '%', the formatter will throw or produce garbled output. It should be logger.debugf("%s", builder) or logger.debug(builder).

findings.title: Test only checks an encode/decode round trip, not DER correctness
findings.body: The test converts the JDK signature to RS, back to DER, and then to RS again, asserting only that the two RS arrays match. A concatenatedRSToASN1DER bug that is symmetric with asn1derToConcatenatedRS would still pass. The test never verifies the converted DER signature with the public key via Signature.verify, and it never checks the DER output against the expected structure or against the JDK's own encoding. Adding a verify step on the reconverted signature would catch real encoding errors.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider() returns whichever provider backs the default keystore type (normally SUN). The method name and the CryptoProvider contract say it should return the BouncyCastle provider. Callers that expect a BC provider will get the wrong one without any error.

findings.title: Most CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: Nearly every method of AuthzClientCryptoProvider (getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getSignature, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory, createECParams, etc.) throws UnsupportedOperationException. Because this provider is discoverable via ServiceLoader and can become the global provider (see AuthzClient.create), any code path that touches these methods will fail with an unhelpful exception. Either these should delegate to a sane default, or the provider should only be active in the authz-client's own scope rather than being registered globally.
